label: first copy step after DEL in short sequences starting with z (echoed z input)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, at the step right after <DEL> (recall_idx 1), when the fed-back input is z, i.e. the sequence started with z and the model has just emitted it. Restricted to short sequences: magnitude is largest for L=3 (top examples are all L=3, e.g. z z c <DEL> [z]), lower for L=4, weak for L=5, and essentially zero for L>=6. Does not fire on z in the original phase, on z echoed at later copy steps, on the delimiter step, or for first tokens other than z (fewer than 1% of activations). Dev F1 0.90, mass recall 0.99.

issues: Minor factual slip: the explanation says sequences whose first token is not z account for 'under 1% of activations'. On dev, first_tok != z covers 4.3% of activations (recall 0.043) but only 0.66% of activation mass. Those activations are weak echoes of other first tokens (w, k, 1, s, f), mostly at L=3. The figure is true for mass, not for activation count.

Precision loss is graded by length, not a hidden sub-pattern: at L=3 precision is 1.00, at L=4 it is 0.998, and at L=5 it falls to 0.72 (test). That L=5 band accounts for nearly all of the 766 test false positives. Splitting the L=5 cases by in_count, next_out (digit vs letter, low vs high index, vowel) or n_digits leaves precision at 0.65-0.82 in every subset, so there is no systematic predictor. The model just fires weakly and inconsistently there.

Misses are scattered and low-magnitude: 289 test steps holding 0.8% of the mass. They are weak non-z echoes at L=3, the L=6 tail (precision 0.03 if L=6 is added) and a few recall_idx-2 cases. No systematic class.

Checks that held: the feature never fires in the original or delimiter phase; 99.6% of activations are at recall_idx 1; z input carries 99.4% of the mass; per-activation magnitude is highest at L=3; there are 82 activations at L=6 and none for L>=7. Test scores reproduce (P 0.863, R 0.943, F1 0.901, mass recall 0.992). L<=4 gives P 0.998 but F1 0.72, and L<=6 gives F1 0.73, so L<=5 is the best length cutoff.
